text: Before optimizing code, you should measure it — guessing where the slowness lives is usually wrong.
The timeit module runs a snippet many times and reports how long it took, accurately.
Running it ten thousand times averages out noise, giving a reliable number.
[chuckle] Its real value is comparing two approaches head to head, on equal footing.
Here we pit a manual loop against a list comprehension, and see which is genuinely faster.
[sniff] Measuring like this settles performance arguments with data instead of opinion.
[sigh] For a whole program, cProfile breaks down where every second is actually spent, function by function.
It shows you the true bottlenecks, so you optimize the parts that matter, not the parts you assume.
[groan] Measure first, optimize second — timeit and cProfile turn performance work from guesswork into science.
Up next, math and random. Comment PYTHON if you want the cheat sheet.
